Article Title: Digital asset firms seek sovereign funds’ backing at Delhi meet
Article Text:
Digital asset companies from BRICS and partner countries will seek a bigger place in cross-border payments and institutional investment

NEW DELHI: Digital asset firms will seek sovereign investors’ backing at a Delhi roundtable this week as India pursues faster, cheaper international payments while maintaining that replacing the dollar is outside its financial agenda.The September 12 BRICS Digital Asset Round Table will bring together 50 industry leaders at The Oberoi. Organiser Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute (SWFI) says investors attending the accompanying iBRICS summit manage $1 trillion across sovereign funds, pension funds and family offices. The figure represents assets under management.Held alongside the BRICS leaders’ summit, the industry meeting will examine linking national digital currencies and payment networks, including India’s UPI and Brazil’s Pix. Separately, companies will explore investment in infrastructure, energy, property and critical minerals through digital tokens representing rights in underlying assets.The payments argument has a practical basis. International transfers can involve several banks and currency conversions, adding costs and delays. Connecting domestic systems could shorten that chain, benefiting businesses and people sending money abroad.RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said on August 11 that BRICS discussions covered central bank digital currencies and fast-payment links, with reducing costs a priority. The options remained under discussion. India has also supported wider use of local currencies for trade.That agenda carries diplomatic sensitivities. New Delhi has said de-dollarisation is outside its financial programme, while US President Donald Trump has threatened 100% tariffs against BRICS countries seeking to replace the dollar.India’s participation in Project Nexus, designed to connect domestic instant-payment systems, shows its engagement extends beyond BRICS. Another initiative, mBridge (Multiple Central Bank Digital Currency Bridge), was developed with China and other central banks to enable payments using central bank digital currencies. These parallel projects suggest that decisions about who governs payment networks will accompany choices about speed and cost.At the Delhi meeting, participants are expected to sign an industry charter covering issuance, custody, settlement and investor protection. Regulators and officials implementing digital currency programmes are expected as observers, organisers said.Linking central bank currencies, investing in tokenised projects and regulating private digital assets involve separate policy decisions. The charter would set industry principles within the rules laid down by governments. For investors, enforceable ownership and reliable custody remain central to assessing tokenised projects.“Until now the allocators of sovereign capital and the builders of those rails have sat in different rooms,” SWFI chairman Lakshmi Narayanan said. The roundtable’s proposed charter seeks to give investors and authorities a shared reference for transactions across borders.
Article Summary: Digital asset companies from brics and partner countries will seek a bigger place in cross-border payments and institutional investment. The september 12 brics digital asset round table will bring together 50 industry leaders at the oberoi.

Article Title: Silver prices crash over 40% from Rs 4 lakh/kg high to Rs 2.35 lakh, but buyers are still staying away; bigger problem yet to arrive as 2,000 tonnes ordered by Indian dealers risk piling up
Article Text:
Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins.

Silver Demand Weakens

Massive stockpiling of silver

Silver’s Spectacular Fall

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

A huge crash in silver prices should have led to a revival in demand, but investors seem to be staying away. And this has raised a fresh worry ahead of the festive season.Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. The situation comes even as silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.In Mumbai’s spot market, silver was trading at Rs 2.35 lakh per kg earlier this week.Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses, making them hesitant to make fresh purchases despite the steep correction in prices!Also Read | A couple sold gold for Rs 20 lakh to buy a home, another family got Rs 80 lakh for a US degree and business: How Indians are unlocking value of idle gold sitting in their lockers "Investment demand for silver ETFs, bars and coins has come down. Internationally, prices are unlikely to cross $100 per troy ounce immediately unless the US-Iran war comes to an end. Silver prices are undervalued," Chirag Sheth, global business head, Public Gold Bullion (SG) Pte told ET. "The continuous war between US and Iran has impacted the solar industry, semiconductor industry and EV industry where silver is used. "The weak demand is also creating an inventory problem for domestic players.Indian bullion dealers and refiners have reportedly placed orders for around 2,000 tonnes of silver, which is currently in transit. The additional supplies have raised concerns over a further build-up in stocks. India imports around 7,000 tonnes of silver every year."With no new investors coming in and no immediate signs of prices going up, refiners and bullion dealers are facing a problem internationally as well as in domestic markets," said James Jose, president, Precious Metals Refiners Forum.Silver prices have fallen steadily over the past seven months, following an extraordinary rally that pushed the metal more than 300% higher year-on-year. In January, silver crossed Rs 4 lakh per kg on the Multi Commodity Exchange for the first time."The market is still digesting the aftermath of the speculation-driven frenzy, and this may be prompting investors to stay away after many of them incurred significant losses," said Carsten Menke, head, Next Generation Research, Julius Baer told ET.The outlook for industrial demand is adding to the pressure, with consumption expected to weaken. "A shift to cheaper alternatives, such as aluminium and copper, has started, and the growth outlook for Chinese solar module makers, which are the biggest industrial users of silver, is not as strong anymore," Menke said.The ongoing US-Iran war has added to the negative sentiment surrounding silver. If the conflict continues for an extended period, investors may remain cautious. At the same time, expectations of weaker industrial consumption could make a rapid rebound in silver prices difficult.Despite the sharp fall, some long-term investors are once again looking at silver as a way to diversify their portfolios."The market has taken full cognisance of the marked decline in silver prices in recent days. Some investors have shaved off their allocation, while others have prepared for fresh acquisition depending on their views and goals," said Nilanjan Dey, partner, Wishlist Capital.Dey said investors who have a time horizon of five years or longer may look at buying silver ETFs in a staggered manner instead of putting in a large amount at one go. Monthly or fortnightly investments could help spread out the purchase price and reduce the impact of short-term price movements.For first-time investors looking to add precious metals to their portfolios as a diversification from equities, ETFs can provide exposure without the need to hold or manage physical silver. However, Dey warned that investors with a shorter investment horizon should not assume that the recent decline automatically makes silver an attractive buying opportunity.
Article Summary: Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the us-iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.

Article Title: Viral video exposes Fortuner owner using button-operated number plate concealer to evade fine; Rs 1.22L in pending challans found
Article Text:
A Pune man was apprehended for using a hidden number plate device





PUNE: An SUV owner dodged prying eyes of CCTV cameras on roads while speeding and skirted challans as he concealed the vehicle’s registration just by pressing a button. The Tathawade man ran out of luck on Tuesday.The Pimpri Chinchwad RTO tracked him down after a video of his Fortuner's auto-hiding number plate purportedly on Pune-Mumbai Expressway went viral on social media. He was fined Rs 4,500 for unauthorised alteration in his vehicle and the amount was collected on Tuesday.Pimpri Chinchwad regional transport officer Sandesh Chavan told TOI, “After the video was circulated, we checked the SUV’s registration number and found that it had been registered with the RTO office here. Checks on the vehicle revealed that a device connected with wires was installed on the registration number plate. The vehicle owner operated it through a button. When the button is pressed, a black shutter comes down and covers the registration number of the SUV. ”A source in the RTO said the vehicle had 55 pending e-challans, amounting to a total of Rs 1.22 lakh. Most of the challans have been slapped on the vehicle owner for speeding.Each time a fine of Rs 2,000 was slapped on him. Chavan said, “We issued the vehicle owner a fresh challan of Rs 4,500 for unauthorised alteration in the vehicle. He has been warned against repeating the offence and advised to clear all the pending fines without delay. ”He said, “The vehicle owner has been called to the RTO this week again with his vehicle. We will thoroughly check all his vehicle documents again. This is a serious case and we want to set an example so that no one tries the same trick.”Dealers selling automobile spare parts said number plate hiders were easily available on different e-commerce websites for as low as Rs 350 to Rs 400. “We don’t keep it as it is illegal. But some vehicle owners order number plate hiders and a few spare parts shops install the same. Some shops even sell it secretly,” a dealer said,requesting anonymity.
Article Summary: A video of his fortuner's auto-hiding number plate purportedly on pune-mumbai expressway went viral on social media. He was fined rs 4,500 for unauthorised alteration in his vehicle. The vehicle had 55 pending e-challans, amounting to a total of rs 1.22 lakh.

Article Title: AI agents may soon be able to make UPI payments for users: How it may work, what will be allowed and what not
Article Text:
What is Unified Agent Protocol

How it may work and what will be allowed

Industry is already moving

NPCI may soon allow AI agents to make UPI payments on your behalf. A Reuters report citing three people familiar with the matter claims India is preparing a framework that would let artificial intelligence agents make small digital payments on UPI without approval for every transaction. The move could make UPI one of the world's largest networks built for agentic payments, and place India among the first countries with national infrastructure of this kind.UPI is already the world's largest retail fast-payment system by transaction volume, according to a 2025 IMF. Data from NPCI suggest the network processed 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore in August, its highest monthly volume yet. Google Pay and PhonePe together account for roughly three-fourths of that volume.The proposed Unified Agent Protocol (UAP) would create a common, interoperable system for registering, verifying and authorising AI agents that transact through UPI. The Reuters report claimed the protocol was expected to be unveiled at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai; however, NPCI has yet to confirm its announcement.UPI was built around a human user approving each payment. Under the agentic model, a user would instead grant an AI agent defined authority such as a spending cap or restrictions on transaction type rather than confirming every purchase, according to the Economic Times.According to Reuters sources, the protocol is expected to draw on two existing UPI mechanisms: UPI Circle, which lets a primary account holder delegate payment authority to a secondary user, and Reserve Pay, which lets customers block funds for multiple debits. Banks currently cap such blocks at Rs 10,000 for up to 90 days, though sources told Reuters this limit may be revisited for agentic use.Low-value, frequent purchases such as groceries are likely to be among the first use cases, with e-commerce platforms well placed to capture early demand, one source told Reuters. NPCI reportedly expects use cases to grow more sophisticated over time, with agents eventually placing orders around sale offers or making investments based on price thresholds.Spending limits, audit trails and identity checks are expected to be built into the system, so that transactions can be verified as authorised and agents confirmed as legitimate. NPCI also reportedly plans to build in a liability framework, though details were not disclosed in the reportSome groundwork exists outside NPCI's framework. Pine Labs has launched its own protocol, P3P, letting AI agents complete UPI payments after a single upfront authorisation. "The consumer authorises once, upfront. After that, the agent browses, selects, negotiates, and pays. No human authentication. No interruption. No friction," the company said. Gullak's gold-savings AI agent already uses P3P.Mastercard completed its first authenticated agentic transaction in New Delhi in June, the report added, while Visa is separately building similar capabilities in India. Meanwhile, Razorpay has also launched an Agent Studio for merchants in March using Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK.Agentic AI is listed as one of three core technology pillars at the Global Fintech Fest 2026, where discussions are expected to focus on establishing an agent's identity, defining its authority and maintaining audit trails as such payments enter India's financial infrastructure.
Article Summary: Npci may soon allow ai agents to make upi payments on your behalf. A reuters report claims india is preparing a framework that would let artificial intelligence agents make small digital payments on upi without approval for every transaction.

Article Title: Meta launches Muse, a personal AI Agent that can do your everyday tasks; company makes a 'promise' after Muse AI Image 'fiasco' that allowed anyone to create AI images with users' Instagram photos
Article Text:
Meta launches Muse, a personal AI Agent that can do your everyday tasks

Meta's security promise

Muse comes hours before Apple's Big event

Meta has launched a new autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) assistant capable of executing tasks such as sending emails, listing a car for sale, and booking travel. The system, dubbed "Muse" and known internally as "Hatch," reportedly serves as the cornerstone of CEO Mark Zuckerberg ’s ambitions to deliver what he calls "personal superintelligence" across Meta's global platform. In a post on X, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg wrote, "Introducing Muse, the personal agent that understands your goals and works 24/7 to get things done for you."Initially limited to U.S. users, Muse will operate through a standalone app and within Meta’s WhatsApp messaging platform. The company that for now, Muse launches on iOS, Android and the web, with free and paid tiers, and support for AI glasses coming soon.Based on the open-source OpenClaw framework, Muse functions by linking directly to a user’s calendar, email, financial services, smart home hardware, and health platforms. Meta noted that users must manually grant permissions for each service and retain the ability to revoke access at any point.Unlike traditional chatbots, each Muse instance runs within an isolated, cloud-based virtual machine designed to emulate an individual personal computer. This architecture allows the software to execute long-running tasks autonomously in the background without requiring continuous user interaction.Incidentally, the Muse AI agent comes despite reported internal concerns regarding how the software handles sensitive personal data. The system’s deep integration with personal data has intensified scrutiny over potential safety, privacy, and operational hazards—particularly the risk of the agent executing erroneous transactions or mismanaging private information.Meta has made a strong security promise including claims of implementing additional security safeguards. According to Vishal Shah, the company’s vice president of AI products, the engineering revisions successfully brought the tool in line with Meta's baseline thresholds for privacy, security, and model performance. "It is impossible to say that there is never going to be a mistake, but every single part of the architecture has been designed to make this as safe, as secure, as private as we can possibly make it," Shah said. Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said the app runs within “its own isolated environment” inside the company’s computing infrastructure, and “never sees your actual passwords or payment details.”In July this year, Meta launched a new AI image generator, Meta AI Image, that allowed anyone to create AI images with users' Instagram photos. Also, if users had a public Instagram account, Meta automatically opted them in.Meta Muse AI assistant arrives just hours before Apple upgrades its voice assistant Siri AI for the chatbot era. While Siri AI is capable of taking some actions, it is not a full blown agentic system yet like OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceXAI and Meta AI offer. Apple is likely to launch it at its September 9 event, along with new iPhones.
Article Summary: Meta launches muse, a personal ai agent that can do your everyday tasks. Ceo mark zuckerberg's ambitions to deliver what he calls "personal superintelligence" across meta's global platform. Muse launches on ios, android and the web, with free and paid tiers, and support for ai glasses coming soon.

Article Title: How Tim Cook pushed Apple into a new era set for John Ternus’ CEO debut
Article Text:
Apple’s foldable iPhone was codenamed V68

Apple is likely to launch its foldable iPhone, rumoured to be called iPhone Ultra, later today (September 9), making the first big change to its phone design in years. The keynote is also John Ternus’s public debut as CEO following his takeover on September 1. While the former hardware executive will be known as the executive to introduce the foldable phone, behind the scenes, the push into this category remains deeply rooted in Tim Cook’s vision.As per a report by Bloomberg, Cook made up his mind around 2020 following a regional tour of Asia. He reportedly observed consumers in China and across the region carrying folding handsets built by rivals like Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies. Cook returned to Cupertino convinced that Apple had to establish a presence in the emerging segment.Citing insiders familiar with the discussions, Bloomberg noted that Cook became the earliest and most vocal supporter of the category, urging engineers to speed up their work. But interestingly, Apple’s hardware labs had actually been researching flexible glass, hinges and folding screens long before Samsung rolled out the original Galaxy Fold back in 2019.The project, however, lacked decisive commercial focus. Early prototypes leaned toward a folding iPad mini that opened into a full-sized slate.Cook’s intervention pivoted the engineering teams away from specialised tablets and redirected them toward building an everyday folding smartphone intended for a wider audience.Known internally by the codename V68, and referred to by several development teams as the iPhone Ultra, the project became one of the most intricate engineering undertakings in the firm’s modern era. The report also said that planners initially aimed for a baseline price of $1,999, hoping to slip just beneath the psychologically sensitive $2,000 threshold, a marketing tactic Apple previously deployed with the $999 iPhone X in 2017.Recent economic pressures, however, have disrupted those targets as due to component expenses driven by memory shortages, internal pricing models have climbed as high as $2,199 for baseline editions. Premium storage tiers could climb toward $3,000, creating a massive pricing difference when compared against the $799 entry-level iPhone or the $1,099 iPhone 17 Pro.Despite the potential for consumer pushback over premium costs, executive leadership took confidence from recent sales trends. Top variants of the existing iPhone Pro Max model already approach the $2,000 mark, demonstrating that loyal buyers are willing to pay premiums for high-end mobile hardware.
Article Summary: Apple is expected to launch its foldable iphone later today (september 9) the keynote is also john ternus’s public debut as ceo following his takeover on september 1. Tim cook became the earliest and most vocal supporter of the category, urging engineers to speed up their work.

Article Title: Skullcandy Method 360 ANC review: Bose did more here than lend a logo
Article Text:
The Rs 11,999 earbuds with two very different sounds inside them

Start with the case, because you will

You stop noticing they're in

There are two pairs of earbuds in here

The rumble disappears, the rest negotiates

What the money buys

Our rating: 3.5/5

We have learned, correctly, to ignore the second name on a pair of earbuds. Some studio, some producer, some legendary audio brand lending its logo to a spec sheet it had nothing to do with. Both parties call it a collaboration and everyone moves on. So the reasonable position on the Method 360 ANC, which carry "Sound by Bose " across the front of the box, was scepticism.That's not what happened here. Bose supplied the drivers, the acoustic tuning, the ear tips and the stability fins, and the app running everything shares its bones with the QuietComfort software. Which is, more or less, everything that decides how a pair of earbuds behaves in your ear. What Skullcandy kept for itself is the plastic and one enormous charging case carved out of it. Hold that division of labour in your head for the next thousand words, because it explains nearly everything the Method 360 ANC does well at Rs 11,999, and every place it comes up short. You will hear Bose's half of this eventually. You have to get past Skullcandy's first.It's a cylinder roughly the size of a fat highlighter, with a carabiner ring up top that doubles as a pull. Tug it and an inner column slides out carrying the buds, with a click that I enjoyed far more than I expected to.Nothing else on the shelf looks remotely like it. That's clearly the brief.It's also big in a way no amount of charm quite talks its way out of. Slim jeans are not happening. The buds seat upside down relative to the logo, in slots where left and right are mirrored from instinct, and the lettering is faint enough that I was still doing a little rotate-and-squint routine after a fortnight. Skullcandy's own support page carries a five-step answer to the question of how to put the earbuds away, which is the sort of detail a design gives up about itself without meaning to.Against that, the clip isn't decorative. It hangs off a bag strap and stays there, the sliding action means the buds can't scatter if you drop it, and I never once had to hunt for the thing down the side of a sofa. Five finishes, including a leopard print I'd never buy and am pleased exists. If you're in the bag-charm phase of life, this is the only earbud case built with you in mind. If you're not, price the inconvenience in before you commit.Past the packaging argument, the hardware is very good. Each bud runs about 11g, which reads heavy and feels like nothing, because the fin takes the weight instead of your ear canal. Three sizes of fin, three of tip. Once you land your combination they hold through runs, a gym session, a flight, a long edit at the desk. Nothing shifted. None of that dull ache larger buds usually start delivering around the two-hour mark.Touch panels are broad and dependable, which sounds like small praise until you count how many Rs 10,000 earbuds still ignore half your taps. All of it remaps through Skull-iQ, four gestures a side, and the app is one of the better ones going: three EQ presets and a five-band custom curve, an ANC intensity slider, low-latency mode, wear detection, Fast Pair, and multipoint that juggled phone and laptop without ever losing the thread. The voice prompts arrived at launch loud enough to make you flinch. A firmware update has walked them back, which counts as somebody paying attention.Out of the box the tuning is pure Skullcandy, and it is not subtle about it. Sub-bass sits on top of everything, the mids fall back a couple of rows, and there's a lift in the upper treble that keeps vocals above water at the cost of turning glassy when you push the volume past two-thirds. Divine's Kohinoor is a great time in this configuration, the low end landing like a fist and the vocal cutting clean over it. This is the sound the brand has sold for twenty years and there is nothing dishonest about selling it. If your listening lives mostly in hip-hop, house or Bollywood dance production, you could leave the EQ untouched for the life of the product and never feel short-changed.The trouble starts when a recording gets busy. Play Radiohead's Weird Fishes and the bassline and drums begin crowding the guitars that make the track worth playing; by the time the whole thing opens up, the layers are stacked rather than spread. Acoustic material suffers a related problem, where the body of a guitar arrives fine and the string detail above it gets thinned out. And there's sibilance, not constantly, but enough that an hour of anything with a bright vocal starts to nag at the top of your ears. This is also, notably, the setting in which you would never guess Bose had anything to do with the product.None of which is the interesting part. The interesting part is what happens when you open Skull-iQ, find the five-band custom curve, and pull the lowest band down four or five notches. It takes about ninety seconds. What comes out the other side is a different product.Suddenly there's air. Instruments occupy separate positions rather than a shared middle, the stage widens well past what Rs 11,999 normally buys, and the tonal balance settles into something close to neutral, which is the last word anyone expected to write about a pair of earbuds with a skull on them. This is where the family resemblance finally surfaces. Anyone who has spent time with Bose's own earbuds will recognise the shape of it immediately: the same unhurried presentation, the same instinct to get out of a recording's way rather than editorialise over it.Norah Jones on Don't Know Why has the warmth of her voice fully intact and the piano sitting a clear step behind it, not smeared into the same plane. Prateek Kuhad's cold/mess holds together the same way, the close-miked vocal staying separate from the guitar rather than sharing a lane with it. Small things you would not expect at this price stay legible: the decay on a cymbal, the shift in a singer's position between verses, the room a recording was made in. The 12mm drivers were always capable of this. The default tuning was simply standing in front of it.Two things hold up under conditions where cheaper earbuds usually give something away. The first is volume. These play loud, louder than you should be using them, and the tuning holds its shape rather than hardening as you climb. More usefully, it also holds at the other end. Bass-heavy buds tend to hollow out at low volume, so late-night listening turns thin and you find yourself pushing the dial up to get the music back. That doesn't happen here; at whisper level the balance stays intact. The second is what noise cancellation does to the sound, which is close to nothing. Plenty of earbuds around this money lose low-end weight or narrow the stage the moment ANC engages, so you end up choosing between silence and fidelity. Switch between the modes here and the presentation stays put, which is the sort of consistency you only notice a week in, and then stop thinking about entirely.What none of it will do is lunge. This is the one real limit, and it doesn't move wherever you set the sliders. Loud passages and quiet ones turn up wearing similar clothes, so music built on contrast comes out levelled off. The long build on Kashmir wants to arrive somewhere, and here it takes a gentle slope instead of a climb. Orchestral material has the same issue, where everything is audible and properly placed and nothing quite swells. Composed rather than gripping. Whether that's a deal-breaker depends entirely on how much of your listening depends on a track getting bigger.You're not choosing between a right answer and a wrong one here. The default is the more fun of the two and the corrected one is the more capable, and having both live inside a single pair, separated by a slider you'll touch once, is a better outcome than most rivals manage with the one voice they've committed to. The order is the strange part. Skullcandy went and bought some of the best tuning work in the business, then buried it under a bass curve to reassure the people who already knew the brand.The codec sheet is the sour note. SBC and AAC, nothing high-resolution, at a price where high-resolution support has quietly become the expectation. In practice the tuning is strong enough that I stopped noticing after the first week, and AAC on a phone is a perfectly reasonable place to listen from. But it's a saving you can see on paper, and if you keep a library of proper files and a player that deserves them, you will bump into the ceiling eventually.Suddenly there's air. My only complaint is that the good one isn't what you hear first. A brand this confident about sound could have led with it.The codec sheet is the sour note. Metro rumble, ceiling fans, aircraft drone, the low hum a city makes without meaning to, all of it recedes. Skullcandy has never been in this neighbourhood before, and for a commute, which is what most people at this price are buying, it does the work that counts.Climb higher and it softens. Horns, platform announcements, a conversation two seats over, these come through with their corners filed rather than gone. Wind is the sore spot; I switched ANC off on runs. Stay Aware transparency does its job with a faint hiss riding along and, at middling intensity, doesn't distinguish itself from ANC as sharply as it might. The very best cancellation still lives on products costing three times as much, which is what you'd expect and no reason to feel shortchanged.Battery is uncomplicated. Nine hours claimed with ANC on, eleven without; I saw around seven and a half at moderate volume, plus two and a half more charges from the case. Ten minutes on the cable returns two hours. No wireless charging. Calls hold up in a quiet room, sound processed but clear, and surrender to a breeze.It's a crowded slot. There are half a dozen capable noise-cancellers sitting within a thousand rupees of this one, several of them with high-resolution codec support and cases that vanish into a pocket, and if those two things sit at the top of your list, go and buy one of them with my blessing.None of them assembles this particular set of virtues, though. A fit borrowed from a Rs 25,000 pair that refuses to budge. A sound with two moods, both worth having, separated by one slider. An app that does more than toggle noise cancelling. Battery that outlasts most of the field. And a case carrying more personality than the rest of the category combined, charged against your pocket space.That's not an accident. Knowing your limits clearly enough to go looking for help, then building the fit, the features and the software to make the most of what comes back, is sharper product thinking than the skull logo invites you to credit. The badge is doing work here. So is everything Skullcandy arranged around it.So, is this worth Rs 11,999? If you want the most technically complete, most compact earbuds the money can find, something else here will suit you better. If you want the pair that sits best, lasts longest, and sounds better than a brand with this history has any right to, these are worth your time. You will make peace with the case. It takes about a week, and then you will notice you have stopped thinking about it, which is more or less what happened with everything else here.
Article Summary: K skullcandy's method 360 anc earbuds cost rs 11,999. Bose supplied the drivers, the acoustic tuning, the ear tips and the stability fins. The app running everything shares its bones with the quietcomfort software. Bose's skull-iq earbuds are priced at rs 11,999. Built-in noise-cancellation means you don't have to worry about it.

Article Title: After social media ban for kids under 16, Australia has more bad news for Instagram, Facebook, Snap and online games companies
Article Text:
After social media ban for kids under 16, Australia has more bad news for Instagram, Facebook, Snap and online games companies as it plans to give users new 'Switch Off' button

Australia wants to put feed choices directly in user hands

Australian government is deepening legal exposure for Big Tech

Following its decision to restrict minors under 16 from accessing social media websites last December, the Australian government is preparing fresh legislation that would mandate a direct “opt-out” mechanism for algorithmic recommendation systems on digital platforms. Under the upcoming “My Feed, My Way” proposal unveiled by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's administration, tech companies must allow Australian users aged 16 and older to turn off recommendation engines entirely, switching instead to feeds that display only content uploaded by accounts, friends and creators they actively choose to follow.According to a report by CNBC, the measure carries severe financial teeth: social networks, artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots, interactive gaming platforms and digital services failing to comply could face civil penalties reaching 109.2 million Australian dollars (roughly $79 million).The draft legislation, released on Tuesday (September 8) for closed industry consultation before being brought to Parliament later this year, requires tech firms to actively prompt every account holder with a notification allowing them to select their preferred default interface. Beyond social networks, the proposal orders developers of AI conversational bots and online video games to eliminate addictive interface mechanisms that target underage users.“This is not about giving government control. It’s about giving people control. It’s about putting choice back into the hands of Australians online. This is sensible, pragmatic, practical reform. It gives users choice, and it will hold the big tech companies responsible for inaction,” said Albanese.While major applications currently maintain varying degrees of non-curated views, including TikTok’s “Friends” tab, Instagram ’s “Following” and “Favorites” options, Facebook’s personal connection feed, YouTube’s subscriptions tab and Snapchat's split layout, Australia’s law would codify direct, persistent user selection into national statute.Australia’s regulatory crackdown lands during an era of courtroom defeats and regulatory liabilities for major social media developers worldwide. In August, Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a massive lawsuit spearheaded by California alongside dozens of US attorneys general over allegations that Facebook and Instagram misled the public about youth risks.As part of that agreement, Meta promised to introduce chronological feed options, enforce two-hour daily screen limits, and remove cosmetic surgery facial filters for minors within months. The company also wrote an open letter to TikTok and YouTube to follow the suit.Earlier this year, a Los Angeles court handed losses to both YouTube and Meta in a personal injury action that found automated autoplay features and infinite scrolling loops harmed the mental health of a young user.California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who directed the nationwide lawsuit against Meta, has also warned that law enforcement officials are now targeting Snapchat, YouTube, and TikTok for similar product safety reviews.
Article Summary: Australian government is preparing fresh legislation that would mandate a direct “opt-out” mechanism for algorithmic recommendation systems on digital platforms. The draft legislation, released on tuesday (september 8) for closed industry consultation, will be brought to parliament later this year.

Article Title: In 2025, Sam Altman set a goal for OpenAI engineers to create 'automated research intern', a year later company publishes a long update
Article Text:
In 2025, Sam Altman set a goal for OpenAI engineers to create 'automated research intern', a year later company publishes a long update

Skyrocketing compute usage and token consumption

Corporate reckoning over ' Tokenmaxxing '

Roughly a year after CEO Sam Altman instructed OpenAI engineering teams to design an “automated research intern,” the artificial intelligence (AI) company has announced that it has successfully fulfilled that objective, while setting its sights on engineering a fully independent AI scientist by March 2028. In a long update released, the AI Lab detailed how autonomous programming tools are overhauling its day-to-day laboratory operations.According to the long note, rather than drafting routine scripts manually, staff members are handing off complex duties to automated assistants, leading to higher experimentation volume, faster software releases and a shift toward supervising AI-generated code. It also said that the technology has also taken over corporate troubleshooting. Daily help requests submitted to an internal IT support desk run by human technicians have plunged by more than 50% since January, as staff increasingly rely on autonomous bots to resolve software problems.While various companies have limited the use of AI, adoption among OpenAI’s core research teams has surged over the past three months, growing at a far steeper rate than anywhere else inside the firm. OpenAI revealed that the median researcher consumed over $600 in computational tokens daily by mid-August, representing a sharp increase from the $162 daily baseline recorded in July.The top 10% of researchers are now utilising upwards of $7,000 in tokens every single day. These financial metrics represent estimated market rates calculated using external API pricing schedules rather than the underlying internal production costs incurred by OpenAI.Notably, in June, Altman disclosed that the startup's heaviest internal consumer processes 100 billion tokens per month. Demonstrating that scale, OpenClaw developer Peter Steinberger, who joined the lab in February, shared an internal dashboard in May showing an estimated $1.3 million monthly usage invoice, though the expense was completely absorbed by the employer.The rapid evolution of programming agents is dividing the wider technology sector between productivity enthusiasts and corporations. While numerous software engineers say handing off baseline tasks to synthetic agents enhances their output, others remain skeptical about the workflow.Early in the year, enterprise firms actively nudged employees to use generative models, setting up internal scoreboards to highlight the most active users. The fueled a “tokenmaxxing,” where workers maximised AI interactions without prioritising practical outcomes.As mounting operational bills began to outstrip measurable efficiency gains, major enterprises pulled back. Tech firms like Amazon and Meta disbanded their internal usage leaderboards.
Article Summary: In 2025, sam altman set a goal for openai engineers to create 'automated research intern', a year later company publishes a long update. Top 10% of researchers are now utilising upwards of $7,000 in tokens every single day. The rapid evolution of programming agents is dividing the wider technology sector between productivity enthusiasts and corporations.

Article Title: AI boom has put several of the biggest American universities are under 'physical threat', George Washington University’s sale of its Virginia campus is an example
Article Text:
AI boom has put several of the biggest American universities are under 'physical threat', George Washington University’s sale of its Virginia campus is an example

George Washington University’s $427 million campus sale for AI data center

University of Michigan builds $1.25 billion AI computing centre

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you agree with the statement that selling campus land can threaten higher education resources? Strongly agree Disagree 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is creating a new pressure point for American universities. This comes as demand for data centers increases the value of large properties with access to electricity, water and fiber infrastructure. American universities that have traditionally used such land for classrooms, laboratories and research facilities are increasingly competing with AI infrastructure projects, creating what former George Washington University professor Ellen Scully-Russ described as “a physical threat” to higher education resources.The George Washington (GW) University’s sale of its roughly 120-acre Virginia Science and Technology Campus in Ashburn, Virginia, to Amazon Data Services for $427 million is one example of this shift. “Universities are large landholders, and there is a land grab going on with the data centers these days,” Scully-Russ told Fortune. The campus is located in Loudoun County, part of Northern Virginia’s “Data Center Alley”, a major concentration of data centers.GW University announced the sale in February but initially did not identify the buyer or disclose the price, citing confidentiality provisions. Amazon Data Services was later identified as the buyer, paying $427 million for the property.The university said the transaction would strengthen its long-term financial position. GW can continue using the campus for up to five years while it determines how to relocate the programmes and offices operating there. A significant portion of the proceeds will be placed into a new endowment, while eligible faculty and staff will receive one-time payments of $2,500 for benefits-eligible full-time faculty and $1,250 for eligible part-time faculty.The sale came as GW faces financial pressures linked to changes in federal research funding, international student policies and broader challenges affecting higher education. The university has said the transaction will support its finances and allow it to invest in its academic mission.Scully-Russ, who joined GW in 2009 to teach and lead a programme at the Virginia campus, said the property struggled to become a central part of the university’s strategy, despite having newer facilities than some at its Washington, DC, campus.​“It never really got any legs, in my opinion,” she said.She also described a gradual reduction in resources at the campus over several years, including faculty departures that were not replaced and the eventual elimination of teaching assistants because of budget constraints. She said faculty and students were not informed in advance that the university was considering selling the property.“There was no transparency,” she told Fortune. “The faculty, the student body, as far as I know, were not even aware that there was a discussion about selling to anybody, let alone to Amazon.”GW held town halls after the sale was announced to discuss the transition of programmes, faculty and staff from the campus. Scully-Russ questioned the timing of that consultation.“It’s kind of like, do you really care?” she said. “Did you care what I thought before you made this decision? Did you care to let me know that this was in the works?”​However, the George Washington University did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Scully-Russ also raised concerns about universities using land for AI infrastructure while federal funding and other financial pressures affect higher education.“We’re chipping away at our higher ed resources to make room for this technology to expand without any accountability,” she told Fortune, “or any other kind of thoughtful progression, which is really a concern for me.”She also questioned the long-term demand for large AI infrastructure projects.​“I think it’s just a short-term bubble,” she said. “We’re just one technological leap away from having those huge ugly buildings being obsolete. Then what happens?”The University of Michigan is taking a different approach to AI infrastructure through a planned $1.25 billion high-performance computing and research centre in Ypsilanti Township.​Developed with Los Alamos National Laboratory, the project is intended to support research in areas including medicine, materials science, clean energy, engineering, and national security. The university describes the facility as a computing centre rather than a commercial data center and says it will support “applying AI and high-performance computing.”The university has acquired land for the project. In 2024, its Board of Regents approved purchases of 19.82 acres and 6.03 acres in Ypsilanti Township for a future computing centre. In 2025, it received authorisation to purchase about 124.7 acres on Textile Road for the facility.The university has also distinguished the project from commercial data centers, saying the facility will focus on scientific research rather than cloud computing, streaming, e-commerce and other consumer or business applications.The planned facility is expected to require about 50 megawatts of power initially, eventually reaching 100 megawatts, according to a university report.The project has faced opposition from local residents and officials. The Ypsilanti Township Board of Trustees unanimously passed a resolution opposing the proposed computational research facility, “declaring strong and unequivocal opposition.”
Article Summary: Ai boom has put several of the biggest american universities are under 'physical threat' george washington university’s sale of its virginia campus is an example of this shift. Amazon data services was later identified as the buyer, paying $427 million for the property.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works



Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies

AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Soon, Aussies could opt out of social media algorithms
Article Text:
Australians could be given the option of opting out of powerful social media algorithms.

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think Australians should have the option to opt-out of social media algorithms? Yes No 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Australians could be given the option of opting out of powerful social media algorithms under new legislation cracking down on big tech, a minister said Monday. The draft law requiring a “digital duty of care” is expected to be introduced to Australia’s parliament this week.It would require firms like Meta to give users the option of turning off algorithms that tailor recommendations to their personal taste.“A lot of Australians appreciate the algorithm, both for the enjoyment they get out of it or the utility they get out of it,” communications minister Anika Wells told national broadcaster ABC. “A lot of Australians will want to choose the algorithm -- but we think that big tech should offer them the choice in the first place, and they should respect that choice.”“We should give Australians more choice over what they should see on their feeds,” she said.Social media firms have long faced scrutiny over their use of allegedly addictive algorithms and stand accused of directing users to sensational or extreme content to keep them scrolling. Australia implemented legislation barring children from social media platforms in Dec, part of a world-first crackdown designed to protect children from online bullying and “predatory algorithms”.The UK, France and others have followed suit. Data last month found that under-16s in Australia were increasing their use of social m­e­dia apps such as Instagram and TikTok despite the ban.
Article Summary: A draft law requiring a “digital duty of care” is expected to be introduced to australia’s parliament this week. Article Title: In 1971, a surfer cut a piece of foam with an electric carving knife; 55 years later, his invention is a household name

From a garage experiment to the Morey Boogie

Why the Boogie Board name still lives on

A leftover piece of foam, an electric carving knife, and a surfer were all Tom Morey needed to create what would become one of surfing’s most recognisable inventions. In 1971, Morey was living in Kona, Hawaii, where he was experimenting with the idea of a small and lightweight craft that could offer a different way to ride waves. He was already an accomplished stand-up surfer, but he kept looking for new possibilities.According to the California Surf Museum, Morey took a piece of polyethylene foam from his garage and cut it into shape with an electric carving knife. He then used his wife’s iron to seal the foam. A copy of the Honolulu Advertiser newspaper left its imprint on the board, giving Morey a way to remember the date: July 7, 1971. That simple experiment would go on to become the Morey Boogie and help shape the modern bodyboard.Morey’s creation was different from the hard surfboards he knew. The modern bodyboard was a soft and flexible piece of foam designed to be ridden while lying on the belly. Morey found that the board allowed him to feel the movement of the wave in a way that a conventional surfboard did not. He saw several advantages in his new creation. It could turn, was durable and lightweight, and could be produced cheaply. Morey also believed it was safe.The idea was simple enough to turn into a do-it-yourself kit that people could assemble at home.The first kits came with two pieces of foam that had to be glued together along with skins for the top and bottom. Morey placed an advertisement in Surfer magazine, and orders soon began arriving.Morey initially considered calling his invention SNAKE (Side, Navel, Arm, Knee, and Elbow). The name was an acronym for the parts of the body used while riding it. But the idea was rejected, and he eventually chose the name Morey Boogie.The name came from Morey’s love of jazz and a style of swing music which was popular before the Second World War. He felt that ‘Boogie’ captured the movement of the new craft.The first production of the Morey Boogie reached the market in 1975. By 1977, the Carlsbad-based company was producing about 80,000 boards a year. In 1979, toy company Kransco purchased Morey Boogie, and the boards began appearing in major department stores across the United States.Morey’s invention helped establish modern bodyboarding as a sport. By the 1980s, bodyboarding had become the fastest-growing watersport in the world, according to the California Surf Museum.Today, many companies make their own versions of the bodyboard. Yet the name Morey has proved that it is difficult to replace. The museum notes that people still commonly call bodyboards ‘Boogie boards', much as brand names such as Band-Aid, Coke, Kleenex and Vaseline have become part of everyday language.

He then used his wife’s iron to seal the foam. A copy of the honolulu advertiser newspaper left its imprint on the board, giving morey a way to remember the date.

Article Title: Watch: 'Driverless' car crashes into police van after internet outage in Islamabad
Article Text:
In a social media post on Monday, Aalijah sought to clarify that his video was not intended to ridicule Zafar or undermine his work and warned that the technology was not yet ready to be considered completely reliable.

A remotely operated driverless car crashed into a police van in Islamabad after losing its internet connection during a demonstration, with footage of the incident going viral and sparking a wave of memes online.According to local media, the incident took place at D-Chowk, a high-security area in the Pakistani capital, where journalist Muhammad Aalijah was recording a video of a technology-based automated-driving system developed by Abbottabad-based technology enthusiast Ehsan Zafar. The car was being controlled remotely over the internet when a sudden connectivity failure caused its steering to malfunction.Footage shared by Aalijah shows him sitting in the front passenger seat as he explains the vehicle's features while it moves along the road. The remotely controlled steering wheel then appears to lose control, sending the car towards a police van parked nearby.Aalijah can be seen attempting to stop the vehicle by pulling the handbrake, but the car continues moving and bumps into the police vehicle.Aalijah later told Dawn that he had been asked by Zafar to report on his technology-based automated-driving innovation. He attributed the crash to a "technical fault" triggered by an internet disruption.“Everything was fine until a technical fault occurred due to an internet disruption, causing the car to go out of control and crash into a police vehicle,” he said.According to Aalijah, the vehicle was operated remotely through internet and satellite connections. The loss of the internet connection during the demonstration caused the car to become uncontrollable.In a social media post on Monday, Aalijah sought to clarify that his video was not intended to ridicule Zafar or undermine his work.“The sole purpose was to raise awareness and urge people to remain cautious until any new experiment or technology has been thoroughly tested, proven safe and established as a complete success,” he said.“This was a message of caution, not an attempt to discredit anyone.”Aalijah also warned that the technology was not yet ready to be considered completely reliable.“The vehicle was being operated through satellite and internet connections, but during external control, it went out of control as soon as the internet connection was disconnected and collided with a police vehicle,” he wrote.He said the relatively low traffic at D-Chowk limited the potential consequences of the malfunction, but warned that a similar failure on a busy road could have been far more serious.“If the same situation had occurred on a busy road, the consequences could have been extremely dangerous, even fatal,” he said.“This video is not criticism; it is a responsible effort to raise awareness and issue a warning by all means, experiment, but ensure safety first,” he added.
Article Summary: A remotely operated driverless car crashed into a police van in islamabad after losing its internet connection during a demonstration. Footage of the incident went viral and sparked a wave of memes online. Journalist muhammad aalijah was recording a video of a technology-based automated-driving system developed by abbottabad-based technology enthusiast ehsan zafar.

Article Title: Copenhagen’s £200m underground Natural History Museum, under construction since 2019, to open in 2027 with eight galleries, 14m specimens, dinosaur skeletons, 3D exhibits and Ocean Hall
Article Text:
Copenhagen’s £200 million Natural History Museum will open its new underground galleries in 2027. (Photo: Natural History Museum Denmark)

Eight galleries will be built underground

The new museum will feature eight immersive exhibitions covering the history of the natural world. (Photo: Natural History Museum Denmark)

The museum’s collection includes around 14 million specimens gathered over 400 years. (Photo: Natural History Museum Denmark)

14 million specimens include dinosaur skeletons

Interactive 3D exhibits will allow visitors to explore detailed digital scans of specimens. (Photo: Natural History Museum Denmark)

Ocean Hall features a huge glass dome

The spectacular Ocean Hall will feature a huge dome made with 1,600 triangular glass panels. (Photo: Natural History Museum Denmark)

£200 million project has taken years to complete

Museum will sit alongside Copenhagen’s Botanical Garden

A huge new underground attraction is set to open in one of Europe’s most popular cities, promising visitors immersive experiences, dinosaur fossils and access to millions of specimens collected over centuries.The new Natural History Museum in Copenhagen, Denmark, will officially open on March 6, 2027, following a major £200 million redevelopment project that has been years in the making.The centrepiece of the project is a series of eight new galleries built underground, creating a vast new exhibition space beneath Copenhagen’s historic Botanical Garden.The eight exhibitions will be titled Universe, Earth, Life, Denmark, Arctic, Biodiversity, Humans and Ocean Hall, taking visitors on a journey through the history of the natural world, according to The Official Copenhagen City Card website.The museum has been designed to combine Copenhagen’s historic architecture with a striking new underground complex.According to architect Lene Tranberg, natural light will reach the underground exhibition galleries through skylights, while the design aims to “engage all the senses”.Inside, visitors will find concrete interiors, curved staircases and large exhibition spaces designed to create an immersive journey through natural history.The new museum connects the Botanical Garden, the existing historic buildings and new architecture inspired by organic forms found in nature.The museum says the project represents a new direction in Danish museum architecture, combining protected historic surroundings with new underground galleries and above-ground structures inspired by nature.The museum is home to an extraordinary collection of around 14 million items gathered over 400 years, including fossils and specimens documenting the history and diversity of life on Earth.Among the highlights are dinosaur remains, including a 17-metre-long Diplodocus skeleton and T-Rex skeletons.Visitors will also be able to explore specimens using interactive touchscreen tables, allowing them to rotate and zoom into 3D scans of objects from the museum's collections.The exhibitions will cover everything from the formation of the Solar System and the origins of species to biodiversity and the rapidly changing natural world.The scale of the new museum can be seen in the construction details.The exhibition halls have walls reaching up to 10 metres high, while ceilings are made using around 180,000 small wooden slats, designed to improve acoustics across the large spaces.The Ocean Hall measures 16 metres wide, 23 metres high and 50 metres long. Its dome consists of 2,000 steel frames fitted with 1,600 triangular glass panels.Remarkably, only two of the glass panes in the entire structure are identical.The museum's welcome hall is housed in a former engine house that was dismantled and reconstructed using original facade bricks and steel lattice structures.The excavation for the foundations reached 15 metres deep and stretched 400 metres in circumference.Plans for the new museum were first revealed around 17 years ago, while construction began in 2019.The project was originally expected to open much earlier, but planning permission and funding issues contributed to significant delays.The exhibition concept was developed by the museum in collaboration with design agency Tinker Imagineers, which won an international competition in 2018. In 2023, the project entered its production phase, with Event Communications winning the contract to deliver the new permanent exhibitions.Christine Wiberg-Lyng, Foundation Director at Aage og Johanne Louis-Hansens Fond, said the new buildings create a sensory setting that supports the museum's core purpose.The redevelopment will add around 7,000 square metres of exhibition space, while another 2,000 square metres will include public facilities such as the shop, ticket office, VILLUM Hall, restaurant, café and dining areas.Around 500 square metres will be dedicated to teaching facilities for school students.Collection storage, laboratories, offices and other staff facilities will occupy approximately 22,500 square metres. Overall, the new museum will comprise around 32,000 square metres, divided almost equally between new construction and renovated historic buildings.Above the underground galleries, Copenhagen's Botanical Garden offers visitors a living museum containing around 13,000 plant species, alongside alpine rock gardens and walking trails.The site also includes the Palm House and Butterfly House, located inside a Victorian cast-iron glasshouse dating back to 1874.The Botanical Garden is free to enter, while tickets for the new museum are listed at approximately £13.22 for adults and £5.75 for children aged three to 17.
Article Summary: Copenhagen’s £200 million natural history museum will open its new underground galleries in 2027. The new museum will feature eight immersive exhibitions covering the history of the natural world. Visitors will be able to explore specimens using interactive touchscreen tables, allowing them to rotate and zoom into 3d scans.
